newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Belgian prime minister Dehaene to visit Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Belgian prime minister Dehaene to visit Argentina.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene will visit Argentina next week to promote his country's growing interest in Argentine privatisations, the Argentine Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.

Dehaene is due to arrive in Buenos Aires on Monday, when he will meet President Carlos Menem, the Peronist leader who has reformed the Argentine economy and thrown it open to foreign business since coming to power in 1989.

"The Belgians are starting to take part in the privatisation process, but because it's Dehaene's first visit they will also sign bilateral cooperation agreements," said a spokesman for the Argentine Foreign Ministry.

As well as the visits to Congress and the Supreme Court demanded by protocol on Dehaene's first visit to Argentina, the Belgian leader will see for himself Belgian companies already active in Argentine industry.

During his three-day visit Dehaene will observe dredging operations on the Parana River, a major regional waterway, by Belgian specialist Jan de Nul and visit the Bahia Blanca petrochemical complex, where Belgian firm Solvay has a controlling stake in PVC producer Indupa.

The Belgian prime minister, who flies on to neighbouring Uruguay on Wednesday is also due to meet the Governor of Buenos Aires Province, Eduardo Duhalde, the ruling Peronist Party's leading candidate so far to succeed Menem in 1999.
